name: Mark Richey Woodworking and Design
old_description: The highest quality architectural woodwork and corporate furniture expertly built for exceptional clients
about:
Mark Richey Woodworking and Design operates from a 105,000-square-foot facility at 40 Parker Street in Newburyport, Massachusetts. The company was founded in 1981 by Mark and Teresa Richey and is certified as a woman- and minority-owned business. Over four decades it has grown into a national provider of architectural woodwork and corporate furniture, with a division called WallGoldfinger Furniture dedicated to custom workplace furnishings.

The shop combines high-tech tooling — CNC routers, state-of-the-art finishing lines — with traditional hand craftsmanship to produce acoustic panels, curved wood elements, custom trim, staircases, museum displays, window walls, and full wall-paneling systems. On the furniture side it builds boardroom tables, conference and dining pieces, desks, credenzas, lecterns, moot-court furniture, banquettes, and collaborative seating, including the proprietary Doko product line. The facility reports thousands of completed projects and more than 3,100 combined years of staff experience.

Clients span academic, corporate, museum, performing-arts, residential, restaurant, retail, and hospitality sectors. Notable installations include the LEGO Group’s U.S. headquarters in Boston, the CarGurus office, Novartis Biomedical Research’s U.S. headquarters, the Met’s 81st Street Studio, and a Midwest contemporary residence designed by Peter Rose Architects.

The founders frame the business around sustainability — the plant runs on clean-burning biomass heat — and inclusivity, aiming to mentor a new generation of craftspeople from historically marginalized groups. Leadership emphasizes fused art-and-technology craftsmanship, integrated project teams, and a promise to meet deadlines without sacrificing quality.
